text:
laura: @incidentbot didn't page oncall for PROD error at ~13:02. Slack thread created but no phone pages. :rotating_light:

mike: seeing it too, our monitoring shows repeated notify-proxy 429s around 13:01-13:04. can you paste incbot logs?

laura: logs from the bot -> ```
[13:02:01] INCIDENTBOT -> POST /page team=payroll payload=<@ben-oncall>
[13:02:01] notify-proxy -> 202 Accepted (queued)
[13:02:01] suppressor -> drop page reason=mention_filter rule=mf-v2-42 matched="@here"
[13:02:02] suppressor -> rate_limit window=10m
```

ops-bot: automatic note: pages suppressed by mention-filter v2 for team:payroll due to repeated @here usage. suppression window=10m. rule id=mf-v2-42.

samantha: that rule was changed in infra last night. it was meant to ignore bot-originated pages but i think the regex got tightened. we introduced a negative-lookbehind refactor.

mike: to confirm — suppressor matched the incoming mention payload incorrectly?

laura: yes. incoming payload contains `<@U12345>` style mention; our sanitiser strips angle brackets before matching, leaving `@U12345` which matches the `@\w+` branch and then trips the `@(?:here|channel)` check due to a subtle grouping bug.

ben-oncall: i didn't get a page. i was only watching Slack — saw the alert message in channel but no phone ring. customer impact?

laura: one enterprise customer hit an embedding generation error and support escalated. looks like mitigation was delayed ~6 minutes while we coordinated.

mike: immediate mitigation — disable suppressor for incidentbot team and push regex hotfix. commands: ```
kubectl apply -f suppressor-disable-temporary.yaml --namespace=notify
kubectl set image deploy/suppressor suppressor=registry.redwood/suppressor:hotfix-mention-20260318
kubectl rollout restart deploy/suppressor --namespace=notify
```

deploy-bot: Started rolling restart for deploy/suppressor (rev=hotfix-mention-20260318).

ops-bot: suppression disabled for team=payroll temporarily (5m window) as requested by @mike.

samantha: i pushed the regex fix to main and added an explicit bot-exempt clause: `if sender_is_bot: skip_mention_filter`. also added unit tests for `<@...>` patterns.

laura: verified a test page to ben-oncall: `page team=payroll message=TEST` -> ben confirmed via SMS. :phone: :white_check_mark:

ben-oncall: got the test page. i also received the manual escalation SMS earlier. thanks.

mike: followups: 1) open an RCA and customer incident notice 2) audit missed pages via PagerDuty export 3) add a feature flag so suppressor defaults to permissive for known bots.

laura: filing follow-up ticket INC-2026-1134 with timeline and customer contact. assigning to @samantha and @mike for RCA and customer comms.

laura: short RCA summary in thread: root cause = mention-filter regex regression combined with suppressor default-on behavior for incidentbot; mitigation = hotfix regex + temporary disabling of suppressor for team; impact = ~6m delay to oncall and one enterprise customer reached support. next steps = add unit tests, explicit bot-exempt rule, feature flag, and run PD audit export.

mike: i'll handle PD audit and attach results to INC-2026-1134.

laura: closing coordination here — will update ticket when customer notice sent. thanks everyone for fast triage :heart:
